abstract: Photonic N00N states enable phase sensing beyond the classical limit, but their generation conventionally relies on interferometric manipulation of photons using bulk optical components. Here we demonstrate the direct generation of a family of tunable two-photon polarization N00N states from a subwavelength-thick 3R-MoS2 flake. For propagation along the optic axis, the in-plane crystal symmetry allows all symmetry permitted spontaneous parametric down-conversion pathway to interfere coherently, while the large second-order nonlinearity provides sufficient brightness at submicrometer thickness without phase matching. The pump polarization sets the basis of the N00N state or equivalently a two-photon Holland-Burnett state without altering its structure or the generation efficiency. The biphotons are highly indistinguishable, reach high fidelity with the target state across a wide range of pump polarizations, and show two-photon interference fringes with visibilities above the threshold for the postselected phase supersensitivity. Our theoretical analysis further indicates that, in the ideal single-mode limit, the same interaction would yield higher-order Holland-Burnett states. By eliminating interferometric stages, our results establish a compact, pump-programmable source for quantum-enhanced polarization interferometry
